note: Staging choices rolled after the format is locked. They work with an original look or, when the user asked for one, a motion-styles card: if the card bans a pick, re-roll that axis with --lock to an option the card allows.

options.label: Problem to solution
options.brief: Show the pain, then the product removing it.

options.label: Before and after
options.brief: The same frame or place shown twice, changed by the product.

options.label: Countdown or list
options.brief: Numbered beats build to the last, biggest one.

options.label: One continuous shot
options.brief: No cuts: one camera path visits every idea.

options.label: Question and answer
options.brief: Open on a question; every scene is part of the answer.

options.label: Detail to whole
options.brief: Start on a tiny detail and pull back until the whole product or world is visible.

options.label: Whole to detail
options.brief: Start wide and dive into the one detail that matters.

options.label: Journey
options.brief: Follow one user, object or data point from start to finish.

options.label: A-B-A return
options.brief: The opening image returns at the end, transformed.

options.label: Cold open on a detail
options.brief: First frame is an extreme close-up whose meaning arrives later.

options.label: Flash-forward
options.brief: Open on a glimpse of the final result, then rewind.

options.label: Title first
options.brief: The headline is the first image, built in the look's own way.

options.label: Mid-motion
options.brief: Frame zero is already moving, as if we cut in late.

options.label: Question on screen
options.brief: A short question or provocation in the first beat.

options.label: Product in use
options.brief: The product is already doing its job in the first frame.

options.label: Loop
options.brief: The last frame matches the first so the video loops.

options.label: Pull back
options.brief: Pull back to reveal everything at once, CTA inside the wide shot.

options.label: Hold on the CTA
options.brief: Settle and hold still on the CTA for a full beat.

options.label: Echo the opening
options.brief: Repeat the opening composition with one telling change.

options.label: Cut on the final hit
options.brief: Hard cut to the brand mark on the last hit of the music, or on the last beat of the timing grid without music.

options.label: Becomes the logo
options.brief: A recurring element turns into the logo (or the wordmark, if there's no logo).
The peak moment at about 60% of the runtime (a style card's native move, if you use a card).
Peak at about 75%.
Peak late, at about 90%, straight into the ending.

options.label: Double peak
options.brief: A smaller peak near 40% and the main one near 80%.

options.label: Brand literal
options.brief: Brand colours as specified; the primary leads across the video, not necessarily in every scene.

options.label: Restraint
options.brief: Neutrals plus one brand colour; the accent first appears at the peak and may stay on the closing CTA.

options.label: Tonal
options.brief: One brand hue across many lightness steps fills most of the frame; other brand colours appear only as small accents.

options.label: Colour fields
options.brief: Each scene owns one flat brand colour; scenes change by swapping fields. A field in the accent colour is that scene's accent use.

options.label: Light
options.brief: The brand's lightest colour (or white or paper) as the ground.

options.label: Dark
options.brief: The brand's darkest colour as the ground; not black unless the brand is.

options.label: Brand colour
options.brief: A saturated brand colour floods the frame as the ground.

options.label: Changes per scene
options.brief: The ground changes between light, dark and colour as the story moves.

options.label: Huge
options.brief: Few elements, each enormous; type and objects crop at the frame edge.

options.label: Dense
options.brief: Packed with detail; many small parts that reward a pause.

options.label: One object
options.brief: One object fills the frame; the camera stays close to it.

options.label: Small in space
options.brief: Small elements in a large empty frame; the emptiness is the point.

options.label: Mixed
options.brief: Cuts between extreme close-ups and very wide views.

options.label: Locked off
options.brief: The camera never moves; only elements move.

options.label: Slow push-in
options.brief: One slow push across the whole video.

options.label: Lateral track
options.brief: The camera travels sideways across a wide world.

options.label: Zoom through
options.brief: Each scene ends by entering an element that becomes the next scene.

options.label: Cuts between fixed framings
options.brief: Wide, medium and close framings, changed by cuts on beats.

options.label: Tilt or orbit
options.brief: Perspective tilt or a slight orbit on flat layers.

options.label: Centered
options.brief: Symmetric compositions.

options.label: Asymmetric thirds
options.brief: Hero on a third line, counterweight opposite.

options.label: Split
options.brief: The frame is divided; halves compare or trade content.

options.label: Modular cells
options.brief: Cells that open, merge and re-tile between scenes.

options.label: Edge anchored
options.brief: Content pinned to edges and corners; the centre stays open.

options.label: One long canvas
options.brief: All scenes live on one big canvas the camera visits.

options.label: Frame within frame
options.brief: Everything happens inside a device, window, page or card that itself moves.

options.label: Even
options.brief: Equal scene lengths on the beat grid.

options.label: Accelerating
options.brief: Scenes get shorter toward the peak.

options.label: Decelerating
options.brief: Fast start, then longer and longer holds.

options.label: Hold then burst
options.brief: A long held moment, then a quick run of shots.

options.label: Call and response
options.brief: Two alternating framings or voices trade scenes.

options.label: Per letter
options.brief: Letters arrive one at a time, 15–35 ms apart; keep these strings to about 30 characters.

options.label: Per line
options.brief: Whole lines arrive together.

options.label: Mask reveal
options.brief: Elements rise from behind a mask or baseline.

options.label: Draw on
options.brief: Strokes draw before fills appear.

options.label: Scale from a point
options.brief: Elements grow from a point in the video's easing.

options.label: From the edge
options.brief: Elements enter from the nearest frame edge.

options.label: Type on
options.brief: Characters appear in order, typewriter style, 30–60 ms apart; keep these strings to about 30 characters.

options.label: Seeded scatter
options.brief: Pieces arrive in a seeded order and settle into place.

options.label: Annotations
options.brief: Circles, arrows and notes drawn in the look's own hand.

options.label: Numbered markers
options.brief: Indices such as 01/04 track progress.

options.label: Crop marks
options.brief: Brackets or registration marks frame the hero.

options.label: Cursor
options.brief: A pointer acts as the narrator.

options.label: Redaction
options.brief: Bars cover words and pull away to reveal them.

options.label: Running counter
options.brief: A running counter (rows copied, a clock, a timecode) sits in a corner.

options.label: None
options.brief: No accent device; restraint is the voice.

options.label: None
options.brief: No footage.

options.label: Background plate
options.brief: Footage graded into the style behind the content.

options.label: Cutaways
options.brief: Short footage shots between beats.

options.label: Masked
options.brief: Footage plays inside type, shapes or cells.

options.label: Old versus new
options.brief: Archival footage of the old way set against the product.

options.label: Texture
options.brief: Footage at low opacity as a living texture.

options.label: Still scene
options.brief: One scene holds completely still for a full beat.

options.label: No ambient motion
options.brief: Remove background drift; negative space only.

options.label: Logo last
options.brief: The logo appears only in the final frame.

options.label: One edge
options.brief: Every element enters from the same edge.

options.label: Traveling shape
options.brief: One shape travels through every scene and becomes the CTA.

options.label: Break the grid once
options.brief: Exactly one scene breaks the layout on purpose.

options.label: None
options.brief: No twist.

lenses.label: Weather map
lenses.brief: Fronts, isobars, a presenter's sweep, a forecast for the data.

lenses.label: Museum label
lenses.brief: Objects on plinths, small wall labels, a curator's hush.

lenses.label: Sports broadcast
lenses.brief: Lower-third scorebugs, replays, telestrator circles, a live clock.

lenses.label: Recipe card
lenses.brief: Ingredients, numbered steps, a stained card, measured quantities.

lenses.label: Transit signage
lenses.brief: Line colours, station dots, arrows, departure boards.

lenses.label: X-ray
lenses.brief: See-through layers that reveal what's inside, a light box.

lenses.label: Sewing pattern
lenses.brief: Tissue sheets, dashed cut lines, notches, numbered pieces.

lenses.label: Shipping manifest
lenses.brief: Crates, stamps, stencilled codes, checked-off cargo.

lenses.label: Picture book
lenses.brief: Big simple shapes, page turns, one sentence per spread.

lenses.label: Field notebook
lenses.brief: Pencil sketches, specimen labels, observations dated by hand.

lenses.label: Departures board
lenses.brief: Split-flap letters, rows that update, times and gates.

lenses.label: Receipt
lenses.brief: A thermal printer feeding a long strip, totals, a tear.

lenses.label: Seed packet
lenses.brief: Planting instructions, growth stages, a packet illustration.

lenses.label: Chess notation
lenses.brief: A board, moves in notation, one decisive move.

lenses.label: Knitting chart
lenses.brief: A grid of stitches where each cell is a symbol; rows build up.

lenses.label: Flight instruments
lenses.brief: Dials, an artificial horizon, needles that settle.

lenses.label: Film slate
lenses.brief: Takes, clapper, script supervisor notes, cut and print.

lenses.label: Postage stamps
lenses.brief: Perforated tiles, cancellation marks, an envelope journey.

lenses.label: Architectural model
lenses.brief: White card massing, tiny people, a model on a table.

lenses.label: Care label
lenses.brief: Small symbols and instructions sewn into a seam.

lenses.label: Music score
lenses.brief: Staves, notes as data, a conductor's tempo.

lenses.label: Hand-painted shop sign
lenses.brief: Sign-painter lettering, gilding, a shopfront.

lenses.label: Origami diagram
lenses.brief: Fold lines, arrows, one sheet becoming a form.

lenses.label: Ticket stub
lenses.brief: Perforations, seat numbers, a torn admission.

lenses.label: Stage script
lenses.brief: Character names, stage directions, a spotlight cue.

lenses.label: Comic panels
lenses.brief: Gutters, captions, sound effects, a page layout.

lenses.label: Microscope slide
lenses.brief: Magnification, a specimen, focus rings, scale bars.

lenses.label: Pinball table
lenses.brief: Bumpers, a ball's path, score reels, tilt.

lenses.label: Cardboard and tape
lenses.brief: Boxes, packing tape, marker labels, a move.

lenses.label: Library card catalog
lenses.brief: Drawers of cards, call numbers, a date stamp.

lenses.label: Lab glassware
lenses.brief: Beakers, measured pours, filtering, a clear result.

lenses.label: Thermal camera
lenses.brief: Heat colours that reveal what's hidden or active.

lenses.label: Whiteboard session
lenses.brief: Sticky notes, arrows, a marker diagram being drawn.

lenses.label: Elevator panel
lenses.brief: Floor buttons, a level indicator, going down or up.

lenses.label: Race timing
lenses.brief: Lanes, splits, a photo finish, a stopwatch.

lenses.label: Star chart
lenses.brief: Constellations joining points, coordinates, a dark sky.

lenses.label: Assembly manual
lenses.brief: Exploded parts, numbered steps, an allen key.

lenses.label: Board game
lenses.brief: A board, tokens, dice, a path to the goal.

lenses.label: Tape measure
lenses.brief: Measurements, chalk marks, fitting.

lenses.label: Radio dial
lenses.brief: Tuning across stations until one comes in clear.
